subject: Clarify default storage: concrete examples for requests vs outputs
messages:
From: Alice Gomez <alice.gomez@orion-health.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick examples: what you keep by default?

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Procurement is asking for a concise set of examples we can include in the security questionnaire so they understand what Redwood stores by default. Can you confirm the default behavior for the four small scenarios below? Short answers are perfect — we’ll paste into our doc.

1) Web chat: user types a patient note, app calls /chat.stream, tokens sent as streaming fragments, then final completion is returned to the client. Do you keep the streaming fragments or only the final completion?
2) Batch embedding job: we POST thousands of patient notes for embeddings — are those persisted anywhere by default, and for how long?
3) Prompt templates with secret placeholders (e.g., {{PHI}} substituted client-side): is the substituted prompt retained when sent to Redwood, or only the template?
4) Real-time KV-cache usage for long conversations: are intermediate KV cache blobs kept after session end?

We’re trying to map examples to our internal retention matrix (security needs one sentence per scenario). Appreciate a quick by-example reply.

—Alice
Alice Gomez

Subject: Re: Quick examples: what you keep by default?

Hi Alice —

Thanks, great set of concrete questions. Short answers below (I’ve kept them one-liners you can paste into procurement). Marissa and Tessa added technical notes where useful; I’m attaching a one-page matrix (retention_matrix_v1.pdf) with the typical hosted defaults — let me know if you need this with your logo for the SOW.

1) Web chat / streaming: we persist only the finalized completion and the original request payload by default. Streaming fragments are transient buffers and are not retained once the request finalizes unless the customer enables verbose debug logs.

2) Batch embeddings: by default, embeddings and input text are stored for 45 days for telemetry and quality monitoring; customers can opt into shorter storage or immediate disable at the account level.

3) Prompt templates: Redwood stores the exact content received in the request (so if you substitute PHI on the client and send it, it is treated as request data). If you send the template only and substitute client-side after retrieval, Redwood does not see the substituted value.

4) KV cache: runtime KV cache is ephemeral and removed after the session buffer is evicted; there is no persistent backup of KV cache blobs in hosted by default.

Next steps: if you need procurement-safe language I can provide a one-paragraph statement and an attestation that the hosted defaults above apply to your trial tenancy; for enterprise/private we can map to your retention SLAs (e.g., on-premises = you control TTLs).

—Kimberly

Subject: Re: Quick examples: what you keep by default? — technical detail

Adding a few specifics so your security team can see the implementation-level behaviors (feel free to pull sentences into procurement):

- Streaming fragments: our serving runtime buffers fragments in memory while the call is active. Those fragments are removed as soon as the request reaches an end state (completed, cancelled, or timed out). The only time fragments are written to disk is when a customer has enabled persistent debug logs (account-level toggle) or when we autosave transcripts for a user-requested export.

- Finalized completions and request payloads: these are stored in our telemetry store for up to 45 days by default in hosted. We use that window for usage analytics, regression detection, and incident triage. Retention windows are configurable for enterprise and Private deployments.

- Embeddings: the raw text + embedding vectors are stored by default for 45 days. If you use the dedicated "do_not_store" flag on a request or are on a Private deployment with local-only mode, vectors are not retained by Redwood.

- Templates vs substituted content: Redwood has no visibility into client-side substitution. Anything included in the HTTP payload is treated as request data and follows the same retention policy.

- KV cache: our KV caches are salted per-session and evicted on session close. There is no persistent object store copy of the KV cache for hosted customers under normal operation.

Implementation note for procurement: we can provide a short attestation PDF that lists the default retention windows, the opt-out flags, and the Private deployment behavior. If that helps your legal team, I can draft and route it through security operations.

—Marissa
